newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen mixed on foreign share limit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen mixed on foreign share limit.

text.p: Domestic institutional investors would unload their holdings but foreign investors would step into the Seoul stock market on Friday, the first day of the latest foreign shareholding limit expansion, brokers said.
The foreign ceiling would rise to 23 percent from 20 percent.
"The impact will be short-lived," said Casey Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland. "The market will watch the direction that domestic institutional interest takes."
The composite stock index closed on Wednesday at 703.23, down 0.82 of a point.
The market were closed on Thursday for Labour Day.
Choi Dong-chul of Ssangyong Securities said foreign buying orders were pouring in for favourites POSCO, Samsung Electronics, SK Telecom and Kookmin Bank.
"Foreigners are expected to snap up newly available shares of these favourite companies," Choi said.
An improvement in trade deficit in April would limit sharp declines, brokers said. April trade shortfall narrowed to $1.5 billion from $2.04 billion a year earlier.
